acceptance_criteria.criterion: packages/core/src/index.mts exports branded TypeScript types Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, and Tick.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: index.mts re-exports Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, Tick as types from nominal-types.mjs; each type is a branded bigint/number intersected with a distinct readonly '__ciclo_brand' literal tag ('Money' | 'Quantity' | 'Price' | 'Rate' | 'Tick').

acceptance_criteria.criterion: packages/core/src/index.mts exports QUANTITY_SCALE as 100_000_000n, PRICE_SCALE as 10_000n, and RATE_SCALE as 100_000_000n, with bigint literal types preserved.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: packages/core/src/nominal-types.mts declares them as top-level `const` bigint literals; dist/nominal-types.d.mts emits `export declare const QUANTITY_SCALE = 100000000n;`, `PRICE_SCALE = 10000n;`, `RATE_SCALE = 100000000n;`, preserving bigint literal types. Runtime tests assert typeof === 'bigint' and value equality.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: At runtime, each Money, Quantity, Price, and Rate constructor or guard rejects non-bigint inputs and accepts bigint inputs without precision conversion.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: asMoney/asQuantity/asPrice/asRate call assertBigint which throws NominalTypeError with a per-type code (e.g. NOMINAL_MONEY_NOT_BIGINT) when typeof value !== 'bigint'; the returned value is the exact input bigint (returned as-is via a type cast, no numeric conversion). Runtime tests cover number, decimal number, string, null, undefined, boolean, object, symbol rejection and bigint acceptance for 0n, -1n, and a 30-digit bigint.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: At runtime, the Tick constructor or guard accepts 0 and Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and rejects negative values, values above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, non-integers, NaN, infinities, and non-number inputs.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: asTick validates typeof === 'number', then NaN, +Infinity, -Infinity, Number.isInteger, and range [0, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER], each with its own error code. Runtime tests cover all listed boundaries: 0, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, -1, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1, 1.5, NaN, +/-Infinity, bigint, string, null, undefined, boolean, object, symbol.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Compile-time fixtures demonstrate that raw primitive values and values of a different brand cannot be assigned to any branded type without passing through its corresponding public constructor or guard.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: packages/core/src/__nominal_types_typecheck__.mts uses @ts-expect-error on every negative case (bigint literal→Money/Quantity/Price/Rate; number 0→Tick; asMoney(1n)→Quantity; asQuantity(1n)→Price; asPrice(1n)→Rate; asRate(1n)→Money; asMoney(1n)→Tick; asTick(0)→Money/Quantity/Price/Rate). Positive cases (each constructor's result to its own brand) are declared without @ts-expect-error and compile cleanly. TypeScript's TS2578 'Unused @ts-expect-error directive' guarantees the negatives are enforced: verified by probe that removing a real error surfaces TS2578. `npm run compile` succeeds.

acceptance_criteria.evidence: nominal-types.mts and __nominal_types_typecheck__.mts import only from './nominal-types.mjs' (same package); no cross-package imports. `npm run boundary` reports 'dependency-boundary: OK. 15 workspace packages validated against §14.5.'

notes_for_reviewer: Brand technique: intersection of the primitive (bigint or number) with `{ readonly __ciclo_brand: <literal> }`. Distinct literal string per type prevents cross-brand assignment; the property does not exist on primitives, so primitive→brand assignment is rejected. No runtime cost.

Compile-time fixture file lives inside the core src tree so `tsc -b` type-checks it automatically. It exports its symbols to avoid any potential `noUnusedLocals` concerns and to make it a real emitted module. TS2578 (unused `@ts-expect-error`) guarantees the negative cases stay enforced if the brand ever loosens.

asTick(value: number) uses `const candidate: unknown = value` before the `typeof` check to accept the reality that JavaScript may pass non-number values at runtime, and to keep the runtime rejection code path meaningful without a redundant-cast lint warning.

Error codes are prefixed `NOMINAL_` to mirror the existing `CANONICAL_` convention in canonical-encoder.mts and to keep them globally unambiguous. Each rejection reason has its own code so downstream consumers (and later ADR-004 helpers) can pattern-match precisely.
No changes to CanonicalEncoder or any other pre-existing exports; index.mts adds new re-exports only.
Package `@ciclo/core` still has no imports outside its own directory; boundary graph unchanged.
payload.summary: Added branded nominal types Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, Tick and their runtime-validated constructors (asMoney, asQuantity, asPrice, asRate, asTick), plus scale constants QUANTITY_SCALE=100_000_000n, PRICE_SCALE=10_000n, RATE_SCALE=100_000_000n, exported from packages/core/src/index.mts. Money/Quantity/Price/Rate constructors reject every non-bigint runtime input via NominalTypeError with granular codes. Tick constructor accepts only integer numbers in [0, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER] and rejects negatives, over-range, non-integer, NaN, +/-Infinity, bigint, string, null, undefined, boolean, object, symbol. Added a compile-time typecheck fixture (packages/core/src/__nominal_types_typecheck__.mts) using @ts-expect-error to prove that raw primitives and cross-brand values cannot be assigned to any brand without going through its constructor, and that constructor results ARE assignable to their target brand. Runtime tests (tests/core/nominal-types.test.mjs) cover exact-value and bigint-typeof checks for all scale constants and every acceptance-listed boundary of every constructor. No package boundary edges added.
